payload.text: /speckit-constitution Establish the constitution for a small command-line tool project. Principles: (1) Standard library only - no third-party runtime dependencies; (2) Exact money arithmetic - all monetary values handled as integer cents, never floats, and no operation may lose or invent money; (3) Fail loudly - malformed input produces a clear message on stderr and a non-zero exit code, never a silent wrong answer; (4) Every requirement is testable - each functional requirement maps to at least one automated pytest test; (5) Deterministic output - the same input always produces byte-identical output.

payload.text: /speckit-specify Build a command-line tool that reads a CSV file of shared group expenses and prints who owes whom in order to settle up. The CSV has a header row with columns payer, amount, description. The participant list is supplied separately as a comma-separated argument. Every participant owes an equal share of the group total. The tool computes each person's net balance and prints a minimal list of payments that settles every balance to zero. All money is handled in whole cents and rounding must never lose or invent money: the payments printed must sum exactly to the total imbalance. Malformed input (missing file, unknown payer not in the participant list, non-numeric or negative amount, empty participant list) must produce a clear error on stderr and a non-zero exit code. Python 3, standard library only.

payload.text: /speckit-plan Python 3.11+, standard library only. Single installable-free layout: a src/splitter/ package with cli.py (argument parsing and exit codes), parser.py (CSV reading and validation), settle.py (balance and minimal-transaction computation), and money.py (integer-cent helpers). Tests in tests/ using pytest. Entry point runnable as python -m splitter. No third-party runtime dependencies.
